numerical_failure.observed_behavior: cauchy ppf at q=0.5 returns -6.123233995736766e-17 instead of exactly zero, because 0.5*np.pi is not exactly pi/2 in floating point (old implementation np.tan(np.pi*q-np.pi/2.0)); tail CDF/SF accuracy was also poor before the arctan2-based rewrite
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: ppf(0.5) should be exactly zero; cdf and sf should keep good relative precision across the whole domain
trigger_conditions: evaluating cauchy cdf or sf in the tails (large |x|)
oracle_clues: issue text shows ppf(0.5) not exactly zero
PR#21335 replaces _ppf with scu._cauchy_ppf(q, 0, 1) and _isf with scu._cauchy_isf(q, 0, 1) (Boost wrappers)
PR discussion says boost handles p=0.5 with zero relative error and p=0.25 within one ulp

numerical_characteristics.precision: Double-precision floating point is implied: 0.5*np.pi is not exactly pi/2, giving ppf(0.5)=-6.123233995736766e-17 instead of exactly zero. The PR says the arctan2-based CDF/SF give good precision over the entire domain. The passages do not state a precision threshold.
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Discrepancy reported at q=0.5 (ppf(0.5)). The PR discussion also references the subnormal input 5e-324, where tan(pi*(5e-324-0.5)) overflows to -inf when stored as a double.
category_specific_evidence: Issue #20761 reports ppf(0.5)=-6.123233995736766e-17 for cauchy, caused by 0.5*np.pi not being exactly pi/2 in floating point.
Original formulas used 0.5 + arctan(x)/pi for CDF and tan(pi*q - pi/2) for PPF; PR #21335 replaces CDF/SF with arctan2(1, -x)/pi and arctan2(1, x)/pi and wraps scu._cauchy_ppf and scu._cauchy_isf.
The PR body says the new CDF/SF expressions give good precision over the entire domain.

Discussion shows mpmath tan(pi*(5e-324-0.5)) overflows to -inf as a double, and Boost handling of 5e-324 was judged correct; an overflow-policy corner case for small p was noted as possibly not a bug.
The passages say no dtype is singled out: the only dtype reference is the double/IEEE 754 context, so no dtype-differential behaviour is stated.

The passages do not state a tolerance separating correct from incorrect answers. The oracle clues (outside the passages) say Boost gives p=0.25 within one ulp and zero relative error at p=0.5, but no tolerance value is given.
Maintainer requested precision-sensitive review: 'We welcome expertise on precision related issues.'
reproduction_risks: Exact-zero expectation at ppf(0.5) is sensitive to how pi/2 is represented; comparing with exact zero fails under the original formula.
Subnormal inputs (e.g. 5e-324) can overflow to -inf in ppf/isf depending on the implementation and error policy.
